CheckTitle: Bedrock AgentCore memory delivers its application logs
CheckType: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Description: **Bedrock AgentCore memory** emits application logs covering the extraction and consolidation jobs that turn session events into long-term memory records, plus `DeleteMemory` processing. AgentCore configures no log destination for memory automatically, so those logs exist only once a **CloudWatch Logs** vended-log delivery for `APPLICATION_LOGS` targets the memory ARN.
Risk:
A memory with no **application-log** delivery keeps no record of how its stored facts were formed.

Extraction and consolidation run inside the service rather than as caller API calls, so **CloudTrail** never sees them: a **memory poisoning** attempt cannot be traced back to the session, actor, or event that introduced the record, and silent extraction failures go unnoticed.

Code.CLI: aws logs put-delivery-source --name <example_resource_name>-logs-source --log-type APPLICATION_LOGS --resource-arn <memory_arn> && aws logs put-delivery-destination --name <example_resource_name>-logs-destination --delivery-destination-type CWL --delivery-destination-configuration destinationResourceArn=<log_group_arn> && aws logs create-delivery --delivery-source-name <example_resource_name>-logs-source --delivery-destination-arn <delivery_destination_arn>
Code.NativeIaC:
```yaml
Resources:
  exampleDeliverySource:
    Type: AWS::Logs::DeliverySource
    Properties:
      Name: example_resource-logs-source
      LogType: APPLICATION_LOGS  # Critical: the extraction and consolidation logs
      ResourceArn: arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-east-1:123456789012:memory/example_memory-EXAMPLE123
  exampleDeliveryDestination:
    Type: AWS::Logs::DeliveryDestination
    Properties:
      Name: example_resource-logs-destination
      DestinationResourceArn: !GetAtt exampleLogGroup.Arn
  exampleDelivery:
    Type: AWS::Logs::Delivery
    Properties:
      DeliverySourceName: !Ref exampleDeliverySource
      DeliveryDestinationArn: !GetAtt exampleDeliveryDestination.Arn
```
Code.Other:
1. Open the AWS Console and go to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
2. Select **Memory** from the navigation pane and choose the memory
3. Scroll to the **Log delivery** pane and choose **Add**
4. Select a destination type (CloudWatch Logs group, Amazon S3 bucket, or Amazon Data Firehose)
5. For **Log type**, select **APPLICATION_LOGS**
6. For CloudWatch Logs, accept the default destination log group or enter one beginning with /aws/vendedlogs/
7. Choose **Add** and confirm the log delivery status shows Delivery active

Recommendation.Text: Create a CloudWatch Logs vended-log delivery for each AgentCore memory: register an `APPLICATION_LOGS` delivery source against the memory ARN, create a CloudWatch Logs, S3, or Firehose delivery destination, then create the delivery that links them. A CloudWatch Logs destination must be a log group whose name begins with `/aws/vendedlogs/`. Set a retention period that matches your investigation window and pivot on the `session_id`, `actor_id`, and `event_id` fields to tie an extracted memory record back to the conversation it came from.

Notes: This check reports one finding per AgentCore memory discovered via ListMemories in each scanned region, so an account with no memory resources produces no findings. A memory ARN is matched against DeliverySource.resourceArns, the only field that ties a delivery source to a specific resource, and a TRACES source for the same memory carries spans rather than the application logs so it is not credited. A region whose delivery inventory could not be listed returns MANUAL rather than FAIL, because vended-log delivery is off by default and an unreadable inventory cannot be distinguished from a disabled one. The collector reading DescribeDeliverySources and DescribeDeliveries runs only when a check that reads it is in scope.
